title: Lyophilized Human Bone Allograft as an Antibiotic Carrier: An In Vitro and In Vivo Study
authors: Coraça-Huber DC, Steixner SJM, Najman S, Stojanovic S, Finze R, Rimashevskiy D, Saginova D, Barbeck M, Schnettler R. Antibiotics. 2022; 11(7):969. DOI 10.3390/antibiotics11070969
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss maxgraft (processed human allograft) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Human bone allografts showed the capacity to act as customized loade d antibiotic carriers to prevent acute infections and should be considered in the management of bone infections in combination with systemic antimicrobial therapy” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
